A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same PG-OMA research. The complete 26-page v1 and 29-page v2, including Appendices A–F, provide sufficient text, equations, figures, and tables for comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original gridworld, MPE, and SMAC simulations, including suboptimal-demonstration experiments and an appendix analysis of occupancy-estimation batch size.

after.justification: V2 retains these original simulation results in Figures 1, 2, and 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same MLE occupancy approximation, pseudoreward construction, and stochastic policy-gradient update. The sampling algorithm and documented network architectures are also unchanged; the expanded MLE discussion introduces no procedural modification.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same gridworld settings with optimal and suboptimal demonstrations, MPE cooperative navigation, and SMAC 3sv4z. Additional applications discussed in the appendices remain examples or future work, not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The count-based PG comparator and discrete-task oracle references are retained. MPE still uses a discretized count-based baseline, while SMAC reports only PG-OMA because that baseline was intractable. The expanded discussion of other methods adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The experimental settings remain unchanged, including the B=100 main count-based comparison, MPE discretization into 20 bins for each of four observation dimensions, evaluation metrics, and the hyperparameters in Tables 2 and 3.

E4.justification: The suboptimal-demonstration tests and the B=10 versus B=100 occupancy-estimation sensitivity analysis are retained with identical plots. V1 Figure 5 becomes v2 Figure 4; no new ablation or robustness analysis is added.

E5.justification: Appendix E relabels its uncertainty paragraph from 'Tolerance intervals' to 'Confidence intervals.' Both versions still specify five random initializations and plotting mean and variance, while v2 Figure 1 retains the tolerance-interval description using mean and standard deviation. This changes reporting terminology without establishing a different statistical calculation.

E6.justification: The empirical curves and findings are unchanged: v1 Figures 2, 3, and 5 match v2 Figures 1, 2, and 4. The removed introductory figure repeats baseline curves retained in v2 Figure 1(b), so no distinct empirical result is lost. The theoretical complexity correction is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Corollary 13 changes the concave-utility global-optimality sample complexity from O(m ε^-3) to O(m ε^-4), also updating Table 1 up to logarithmic factors. Although the parameter choices and appendix proofs remain unchanged, this materially revises a principal theoretical guarantee and corrects its stated dependence on accuracy.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens its characterization of prior unified RLGU approaches from 'mainly' focusing on tabular settings to 'only' doing so. The central contributions—PG-OMA, dimension-dependent occupancy estimation, stationarity and global-optimality guarantees, and scalability demonstrations—otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A extend the existing MLE-versus-MSE rationale with initial-distribution coverage arguments and claims concerning consistency, efficiency, scaling, outliers, and distribution constraints. They also explain model-free advantages and additional assumption tradeoffs. The interpretations of experimental results and Appendix F's limitations and future directions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same hardware description, actor/critic/discriminator architectures, occupancy approximation details, preprocessing, hyperparameters, and fine-tuning information. Architecture descriptions move relative to the gridworld illustration but are not newly disclosed. No new code or data access information appears.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against Barakat et al. (2023) and Mutti et al. (2023), adding Section 5 and further arguments in Appendix A beyond the comparisons already present in v1. It removes the detailed comparison explaining complementarity with Huang et al. (2023), although that work remains cited, and adds Bai et al. (2022).

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, shortens several section headings, inserts a dedicated prior-work comparison, formalizes Appendix E subsections, and edits captions and bibliography style. Most existing methodological, experimental, and proof prose remains intact; the revisions do not constitute extensive rewriting of the whole document.

P2.justification: V2 removes the redundant introductory Figure 1 and renumbers the retained figures, with caption and placement adjustments. The remaining plot graphics and table structures are preserved; the changed complexity entry in Table 1 is a theoretical correction rather than a display redesign.

improvement.justification: Correcting Corollary 13 and Table 1 removes an overoptimistic complexity claim: the retained iteration and sampling choices imply m ε^-4 up to logarithms. More explicit assumption comparisons also aid assessment. These gains are limited by removal of the detailed Huang comparison and inconsistent confidence-versus-tolerance terminology. The method and empirical support remain unchanged.
